pending_verification.claim: Lap-cost measurement can survive the window-roll check. VERIFIED 2026-08-09T06:59Z.
pending_verification.verified: record-lap --phase=end classified a lap spanning the 06:41:57Z -> 06:58:41Z collections as usable. Under the old string comparison the same lap would have been discarded as window_reset_mid_lap, because resets_at moved .314Z -> a fresh value. That branch is no longer the blocker.
pending_verification.but_still_unmeasured: The very first surviving sample measured 0.000% and wrote avg_cost_percent 0 into state/automations.json, which is worse than null: pacing would reserve nothing and let the automation eat the pool unaccounted. Both ends read 43% because read-claude-usage.mjs rounds to one decimal, and the five_hour window also sat unchanged at 4%/96%, which looks like upstream reporting lag rather than a free lap. That sample is now reclassified below_measurement_resolution and the registry entry is back to null.
pending_verification.next_blocker: resolution, not classification. A lap budget is 1.37% and the reading resolves to 0.1%, so a single lap sits near the noise floor. Two routes, neither tried: measure across several laps instead of one (start once, close after N fires), or find a usage field with finer granularity than the rounded percentage.
pending_verification.indicator: state/automations.json shows avg_cost_percent != null with samples >= 1 for any claude-trigger automation, and scripts/pacing.mjs stops printing UNMEASURED default for it.
pending_verification.why_it_matters: pacing.mjs reserves 0.5% per run for three unmeasured automations — 81% raw, capped to 30.10% — against a 12.90% discretionary pool. Every lap budget is a residue of that guess.
